# frontend

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/frontend"
```

Package frontend reads TGo source for the type checker.

Go's parser cannot read TGo operators such as fetch\(\)\! or conditional expressions such as if and switch. The frontend temporarily replaces added syntax with forms that Go's standard parser can read. It returns a syntax tree: a structure that describes the expressions, statements, and declarations in the file.

The result also records which parts of that tree represent TGo operations. These records let the [checker](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/checker/readme.md>) apply TGo rules instead of treating the replacement forms as ordinary Go calls. The frontend does not decide types or generate the final Go code.

### Preserve the meaning of source positions and statements

Temporary text can be longer than the original expression. The frontend maps positions back to the input so errors refer to the TGo text that the user wrote. The physical Go filename remains available for Go's file selection.

Some replacement forms contain function literals to hold branch statements. These forms do not introduce a function in the source program. For example, a return inside a conditional expression still exits the enclosing source function. The checker and [lowering](<https://github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/blob/main/internal/lowering/readme.md>) must preserve that rule.

A comprehension builds a slice or map from range loops and optional filters. Its records preserve the order of those clauses and the output expression. This lets later compiler steps check names and types in the same scope that the source program defines.

## func MarkPostfix

```go
func MarkPostfix(filename string, input []byte, used map[string]bool, operations map[string]Marker) []byte
```

MarkPostfix replaces postfix \! and \!\! with named comments that Go can parse. It reserves fresh names in used and records each operator in operations.

## func MarkerExpressions

```go
func MarkerExpressions(fset *token.FileSet, file *ast.File, operations map[string]Marker) map[ast.Expr]Marker
```

MarkerExpressions matches recorded comments to calls in the parsed file. It records the source call name and panics if an operator does not follow a call.

## func WrapMarker

```go
func WrapMarker(file *ast.File, expression ast.Expr, operation Marker)
```

WrapMarker replaces the selected expression with a marker call for source checking. It changes file in place and removes the comment for this operation.

## type Comprehension

Comprehension records a typed collection and its range and filter statements. Output identifies the leaf call that supplies an element or a key and value.

```go
type Comprehension struct {
    Position token.Position
    Type     ast.Expr
    Body     *ast.BlockStmt
    Output   string
    Ranges   []*ast.RangeStmt
}
```

## type Marker

Marker records a postfix operation in Go\-compatible source.

```go
type Marker struct {
    Name     string
    Wrap     bool
    CallName string
    Position token.Position
}
```

## type Parsed

Parsed contains Go syntax and records for the added TGo expressions.

```go
type Parsed struct {
    File           *ast.File
    Comprehensions map[string]*Comprehension
    Conditionals   map[string]token.Position
    Propagations   map[string]Marker
}
```

### func ParseFile

```go
func ParseFile(fset *token.FileSet, filename, sourceName string, input []byte, used map[string]bool) (*Parsed, error)
```

ParseFile parses added expressions and maps syntax positions to the input. Conditional bodies remain statements in the original enclosing function.
